AccessStatus.description:
Access status for an external source attachment.

Indicates whether the current user can access the attached resource.

Access checking is on-demand - we only verify actual access when the user
explicitly clicks "Check Access". On initial load, we only check if the user
has a connection to the provider.

Attributes:
    accessible: Access status:
        - None: Connected but not yet verified (user should click "Check Access")
        - True: Access verified (user clicked Check Access and it succeeded)
        - False: No access (not connected, or Check Access failed)
    reason: Status reason:
        - 'not_connected': User hasn't connected this provider
        - 'connected': User has provider connected but access not verified
        - 'verified': Access verified via Check Access
        - 'no_access': User's token can't access this resource
        - 'not_found': Resource no longer exists
    message: Human-readable message explaining the access status.

SourceOut.description:
Response model for citation sources.

Uses stable keys (e.g., "pmid:12345678", "rag:abc123de") for citation mapping.
Citation tokens in content use format {{key}} like {{pmid:12345678}}.

``canvas_sources`` are stored verbatim (see ``get_canvas``), and connectors
enrich them with many optional locator fields the frontend needs to build
"open" links: knowledge/wiki targets (``kg_document_id``, ``kg_entity_id``,
``page_id``/``wiki_page_id``/``knowledge_page_id``, ``section_id``,
``section_title``, ``entity_type``), file locators (``local_path``,
``image_url``, ``slide_number``), and provider ``meta``. Declaring each here
would silently drop any the model does not yet know about, so we mirror the
verbatim-passthrough contract with ``extra="allow"``: unknown keys survive
serialization instead of being stripped, and the few fields below keep their
coercion/derivation. Root cause this guards: knowledge sources arrived with
``page_id``/``kg_document_id`` stripped, so the canvas source popover could
not link back to the wiki page or entity.

Ask one person for an interview.

For a member of the organization (``recipient.user_id``, with ``project_id``)
the request lands in their interview inbox and they are notified. Only a
project owner or admin may ask, and only a member who can take part in the
project's interviews may be asked (422 otherwise, the same answer for an
unknown id or a person in another organization).

For anyone else (``recipient.email``) Beakr saves a sendable interview, makes
a link for them and emails it. The email is never matched to an account.
PHI organizations cannot send outside Beakr (403); a sandbox organization
never sends real email (``email_status: not_sent_sandbox``); one person may
make at most 50 interview links a day (429).
